I remember when Rocket League was first launched. I hadn't played the original game, "Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle Cars" (or heard of it), but seeing a game launch on PS Plus as a heady mix of football, cars and neon lights grabbed my attention. Since then, I've suffered a mild addiction to 2vs2 ranked matches, which I'd like to break free of but know I won't. Other modes are available beyond 2v2 ranked, I'm assured of this and can see it in the menu system, but I assume they're reserved for people even more disturbed than me. 
I'd like to be clear, this is a very fun game. 5 minute matches are the perfect length, especially for those in households where shouts of "5 minutes!" is accepted currency for pushing back household chores or parental responsibility. The general gameplay loop is largely perfect. It absolutely should be and is this fun to chase a giant ball around in a car, launching in to the air to prevent a last minute equaliser on the line. There's also an extremely high skill ceiling of which I'm still very, very, very far from hitting which captures that "just one more" feeling. You know, the kind of feeling that is generally produced by ingesting illicit substances.
Spend anytime watching clips on YouTube, or maybe go beyond the rank that you're accustomed to, and you'll soon realise that you're not very good, and you'll probably never amount to anything, but that's ok. If at first you don't realise you're not very good and probably never amount to anything, then your team mates will alert you to this at the earliest opportunity. 
It's a shame Epic are too insecure to let Steam list this game anymore, as a result I'm not sure I'm writing this review for anyone but the community. And to that community I say this: Thank you for being there with me for 5 minutes at a time. Thank you for telling me I'm terrible. Thank you for telling me how well you know my mum. Thank you for letting me know that I should uninstall - I should. I really, really should.

Let this game be a reminder that greed can ruin anything.

Literally fumbled a game that could have mimicked csgo's longevity and economy. Instead an amazing community on both competitive and creative sides were nothing more than mindless consumers to anyone who ever had ownership of this game. 

Its hard to imagine now, but when this game had the recipe to be great, there was real reason to have an hour count like mine. It wasn't just clips on TikTok, there was true incentive to "go pro". The most significant aspect of this was scholarships being given out for college teams across the world as this game had the Recipe to grow so much. As much as it was still the addiction as it is today, there were a lot more healthy takeaways that could genuinely lead to other success in life and not just kids dropping out of middle school.

I'm grateful i got to be a part of the good bits and I'm even happier I didn't stick around to watch this game devolve into the nightmare it is today. save yourself the trouble. I hate to sound like a boomer here but don't waste your time kids. the only reason this game is still breathing is because kids wont stop paying 20$ for something that has no real value. Don't let greed win. nobody actually cares what your car looks like that literally just bots on the internet persuading you to get your parents cc.
